title: Introduce progressive lightweight trace sampler to cap tracing client overhead
creator: Chen Li
description:
Problem: In high-QPS services the tracing client and tail-based sampler are causing intermittent CPU/heap spikes and introducing synchronous IO on hot paths when emitting spans. This leads to p50/p95 latency regressions and occasional OOMs in edge cases where many long-running requests are buffered for tail-sampling. Goal: implement a low-overhead, progressive sampling system that keeps error/long-tail fidelity while bounding memory and CPU overhead to negligible levels (<1% added p50 latency for typical workloads).

Proposal: ship a two-tier progressive sampler + tracing hooks: 1) Inline probabilistic sampler for the hot path (nanosecond-level decision, fast PRNG + atomic token-bucket) that adheres to global and per-route rates. 2) Background adaptive reservoir for candidate tail events and errors: only traces that pass lightweight heuristics (error flag, status>=500, duration > dynamic threshold, or outlier op counts) are admitted to a small reservoir for deferred full sampling. 3) Replace synchronous span flush on hot path with lock-free ring buffer + batched async shipper to avoid IO backpressure. 4) Add early decision tracing hooks so middleware can react (e.g., annotate logs with sample decision) without materializing full spans. 5) Expose dynamic config via Console (runtime flags for base probability, reservoir size, duration threshold) so SRE/PM can tune in prod.

Non-goals: this ticket does not implement policy UI or integrator-side aggregator changes; focuses on client runtime changes and Console runtime flags only.

Success criteria: - p50 latency increase <1% and p95 <3% on load where baseline previously saw +10-40% spikes. - Peak heap allocated for tracing remains bounded (target <3MB per instance under 100k rps). - Effective sampling preserves >=95% of error traces and >=90% of >99th-percentile duration traces in benchmarks. - No synchronous IO on main request path.

Risks & mitigations: - Under-sampling rare bugs: keep error events always-sampled, allow manual pinning via trace hooks. - Misconfiguration causing excessive sampling: circuit-breaker that caps global admit rate at 1% of requests unless explicitly escalated. - Compatibility: maintain existing span schema and OTLP compat; opt-in telemetry toggles to revert quickly.
comments: 2026-02-12 Chen Li: Triage - observed multiple customer incidents where tracing client spikes coincided with increased p95 latency. Root cause points to tail-sampling buffering and synchronous flushes on span backpressure. Filed ENG-14102 to design low-overhead approach.

2026-02-18 Riley Morgan: Design review completed. Decided on hybrid inline probabilistic sampler + small reservoir for tail/error traces. Agreed to implement lock-free ring buffer for span handoff and a single background worker for reservoir selection to bound memory. Action: prototype to validate overhead numbers.

2026-02-24 Chen Li: Prototype results: inline sampler adds ~0.6% to p50 and ~1.4% to p95 in our microbench harness at 50k rps. Reservoir handling (size=1024) kept mem <2.6MB. Observed edge case with bursty errors where reservoir eviction policy favored recent traces leading to drop of rare mid-frequency errors; updated eviction to bias by severity and duration.

2026-03-01 Riley Morgan: Implementation PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4392 - includes sampler, ring buffer, reservoir logic, and Console runtime flags. Unit tests + integration tests added. Leaving for review.

2026-03-03 Natasha Green (SRE): Review - asked for additional metrics: effective_sample_rate, reservoir_fill, reservoir_evictions, async_flush_latency_hist. Also requested a canary rollout plan and circuit-breaker default config. Added as follow-up tasks in comments.

2026-03-06 Chen Li: Addressed review comments: added metrics and default circuit-breaker (max_admit_rate=0.01). Fixed a race uncovered by stress test by switching to a sequence-number-based ring buffer reader. Updated PR.

2026-03-08 Riley Morgan: QA - ran 72-hour canary on staging at 1% of prod traffic. Observability showed steady metrics, reservoir eviction under expected thresholds, and no p95 regressions. Found one case where the inline sampler's PRNG seeded identically across small containers causing correlated sampling; fixed seed derivation to include instance id.

2026-03-11 Chen Li: Load test at 100k rps with synthetic tail events: results - error trace retention 99.4%, >99th duration retention 91.7%, p50 latency +0.7%. Heap remained under target. Preparing rollout plan to ramp to 10%/50%/100% over 3 days with automatic rollback if error retention drops below 90%.

2026-03-13 Riley Morgan: Merged PR and started staged rollout. Monitoring dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/trace-sampling/trace-sampler-health. Early telemetry looks good; will keep ticket open for post-rollout verification and follow-up for UI work.
2026-03-13 Natasha Green (SRE): Post-deploy note - saw small discrepancy in effective_sample_rate metric tagging for older clients; filing ENG-14115 to add versioned metrics and backfill docs.
2026-03-13 Chen Li: Post-merge follow-ups: 1) add doc snippet for SDK upgrade notes in dev portal; 2) add smoke test that asserts no synchronous IO on request path. Added to backlog as subtasks.
